name: a3-recovered-episode-boundary
notes: A3 (P3, reviewed post-fix contract): the first pressure episode recovered at T+2s, so it is history and independent of the second episode.
Exactly one ESCALATES_TO edge reaches the limit - from the second pressure start inside the same reopened episode. No causal or escalation edge may cross the recovered episode boundary.

The unrecovered limit is a severe unresolved condition: it gets its own failure analysis with root cause UNKNOWN and the known escalation chain (5.1, 5.6 oom-chain row: the reopened episode's onset is the contributing factor).
Today the audited engine emits TWO escalation edges (both starts tie to the limit), leaves episode numbering unincremented after recovery, and produces no limit analysis at all.
If the fix version-bumps the escalation rule id (4.18), this expectation updates in the same change.
Episode numbering itself is not asserted here; the post-fix limit analysis shape is.

Re-audit 2026-10-28 (principal, causal-semantics.md §5.2 clarified): a failure is never its own candidate, and an escalation-only path is the anchor's own episode (known chain), not a contributing factor. Suspected-kill/write-failure alternatives explain exit failures only, never a condition anchor.
